Module 3 Project, Part E: Check Your Numbers

This is the output of one complete run of the project, with a fixed random seed. Use it to see whether your own results are in the right ballpark: the same order of magnitude, the same conclusions, the same first digit or two. It is not an answer key. There is no code and no explanation here, and the exam asks about your project, not this one.

What should match, and how closely:

  • Exact values do not depend on random numbers and should match to every digit shown: the group sizes, the observed nearest-neighbor counts, the SDs, \(r\), dCor, the dCov ratio, the table, the midranks and the wilcox.test \(p\)-value.
  • Permutation results vary from run to run. Your null means and \(p\)-values should agree with these to about two significant digits, and lead to the same conclusions at 5%.
